data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Append-only identity is never corrupted by resumption per se; corruption only occurs if the resumption re-evaluates or rewrites already-committed events. Therefore resumption is always permissible as long as the continuation starts strictly after the last committed event, regardless of whether the logical reasoning unit was complete.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If downstream consumers assume that the event stream represents a complete, logically coherent trace, then a mid-unit resumption produces a semantically incoherent stream even though it is structurally valid append-only.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the reasoning workflow contract requires that the event log be a valid transcript of a single uninterrupted run, then any resumption violates the workflow contract regardless of append-only preservation.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If causal identity includes 'single-run continuity' as a constitutive property, then resumption after interruption changes the identity of the whole.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Append-only is a storage invariant, not a semantic invariant. Each event is committed atomically with a content hash and predecessor link. The causal chain is a linked list; appending a new node after any committed node preserves the list's integrity. The logical incompleteness of the reasoning (e.g., a chain-of-thought cut mid-argument) is a semantic property orthogonal to the append-only storage identity. The resumed event simply declares itself as a continuation after event N, and the log remains valid.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
